newsitem.title: INDIA: No cargo diverted from India's JNPT port-official.
newsitem.headline: No cargo diverted from India's JNPT port-official.

text.p: No ships were diverted or cancelled at an Indian port where a fire on December 29 disrupted operations, a port official said on Tuesday.
"The first shipment of foodgrains for the year is expected on January 23," R. Vasudevan, chairman of the Jawaharlal Nehru Port Trust (JNPT), a Bombay port, said.
"It is a cargo of 60,000 tonnes of wheat from Australia," he said. "We are trying to get at least one conveyor belt in operation before that."
"There is no question of ships being cancelled," he added. "No ships have been diverted. We are down but not out."
A fire on December 29 damaged the conveyor belts for mechanised handling of bulk cargo, affecting port operations.
JNPT has three conveyor belts for mechanised handling of bulk cargo, one each for handling urea, sulphur and foodgrains.
Vasudevan said soon after the fire broke out, makeshift arrangements were been made and unloading went on.
"At the moment we are unloading about 2,500 tonnes of urea per day through our alternative arrangements," Vasudevan said.
Of the two terminals at the port, the container terminal had been unaffected by the fire, he said.
This terminal had three berths of which one, the multi-purpose service berth escaped damage, he said.
"Of the other two, we are using ship's gear to unload directly in one berth and in the other, we have rigged chutes to unload cargo from the ships," he said.
